subject.title: feat(memory-core): skip tool construction for dreaming narrative subagent runs (no-tools mode from #93756 review guidance)

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose a plugin-owned `disableTools` capability through the Gateway `agent` protocol for narrative-only subagent runs?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but it expands both the plugin runtime API and the generated Gateway client contract; choosing whether that generic capability should exist is a product and ownership decision, not a safe mechanical follow-up.

options.title: Accept the plugin-owned no-tools contract
options.body: Keep the additive protocol field and preflight reservation, with maintainer acceptance that installed plugins may request tool-free internal subagent runs.

options.title: Use a narrower existing execution path
options.body: Rework memory-core to use an already-approved internal no-tools mechanism if one can avoid broadening the plugin and Gateway contract.

recommendation.title: Accept the plugin-owned no-tools contract
recommendation.body: Keep the additive protocol field and preflight reservation, with maintainer acceptance that installed plugins may request tool-free internal subagent runs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidence-backed recent contributor in the supplied context for the adjacent scheduled internal-run boundary; direct API ownership remains uncertain.
